literal_meaning: দিক বা আকাশে বস্ত্র পরিহিত (clothed in space or directions)
figurative_meaning_en: the naked or space-clothed form of Goddess Kali
example_sentences_in_bangla: মায়ের দিগবসনা রূপে ভক্তিরান্ধ হয়ে ওঠে মন।
রামপ্রসাদের গানে দিগবসনা কালীর চিত্র অপরূপ।
example_sentences_in_english: The digbosona form of the Mother makes the mind blindly devoted.
In Ramprasad's songs, the image of digbosona Kali is exquisite.
history: This expression originates from the devotional songs (Ramprasadi) of the 18th-century Bengali poet Ramprasad Sen, who vividly describes the wild, disheveled, and space-clothed (digbosona) form of Goddess Kali as a symbol of her untamed divine beauty.
note: Primarily used in Shakta devotional contexts to evoke the fierce yet maternal aspect of Kali.
